info.title: corvus
info.description: MCP server and command line for reverse engineering .NET assemblies and native PE, ELF and Mach-O binaries: decompile, search, compare builds, patch and save. By default nothing is executed.

commands.name: batch
commands.description:
Read one file with fixed read-only steps (summary, container, strings, yara) into
one corvus.batch/1 document. --rules <file|folder>, --time-limit S,
--limit containerFiles=N, --limit strings=N, --limit yaraMatches=N.

commands.name: call
commands.description:
The same. Values: name=value (typed by the parameter), name:=<json>, name=@file,
name=@- (stdin); or --args '<json object>' (also --json '{...}'), --args-file F|-.
--load PATH preloads (repeatable); any server option applies (docs/configuration.md).
--json          print {tool, isError, text, structured, error}
--structured    print only the structured content

commands.name: completion
commands.description:
A completion script for bash, zsh or pwsh.
Tool exit codes: 0 success, 1 tool error, 2 usage or invalid_argument, 3 engine missing or unsupported,
124 timeout, 130 cancelled (Ctrl+C).

commands.name: config
commands.description:
Print the configuration to add by hand (for clients not listed).
--dev-reload DIR  the relay's configuration (see install)

commands.name: describe
commands.description: A tool's or prompt's description, parameters and an example (help <name> too).

commands.name: install
commands.description:
Register the server with MCP clients, then start it once to check it works.
Existing registrations are refreshed. Detected clients without one are listed in a
plan and added after one confirmation (Enter = yes); without a terminal they are
added only with --yes (or CORVUS_YES=1) or --all-detected.
--client X      only these clients (repeatable or comma-separated), detected or not
--dry-run       print the plan and write nothing (--check also runs the server check)
--json          print the plan and result as JSON (needs --yes to add new clients)
--strict        write nothing when any client's file cannot be read
--no-check      skip the server check
--command PATH  register this program instead of the running one
--dev-reload DIR  local development: register the relay, which runs the server
published in DIR (./publish.ps1) and switches to each new publish
--skill         also write the agent skill for clients that read skills; skills
written earlier are kept current by every install and update
--enable        turn on an entry the client has turned off (its switch, disable
lists, Claude Code's per-project list); otherwise it is kept off
--set S         add a security switch to every entry, e.g. --set allow-live-attach
--unset S       remove it (docs/configuration.md lists the switches)
--project DIR   with --set/--unset: only this folder's Claude Code entry,
made from the global one when the folder has none
--with-live     install the tested Frida into a private Python environment now
and --set live-install-frida (sessions use it)
uninstall [client...] Remove the registration from every client (or the named ones). With no names it
also deletes an installed copy's program files; --keep-files keeps them. Your data
(annotations, caches, symbols) is kept; --purge-data deletes it as well.
Skill folders written by install --skill are removed.
--dry-run and --json as for install.

commands.name: prompts
commands.description: List the prompts; prompt <name> [name=value ...] prints one, ready to pipe.

arguments.name: PLAN_PATCH
arguments.description:
Find the right patch point for a behaviour change, preview it, apply it and save a patched copy.
goal, assembly?

arguments.name: FIND_FEATURE
arguments.description:
Locate the code that implements a behaviour, starting from strings, names and constants.
feature, assembly?

arguments.name: ANALYZE_ASSEMBLY
arguments.description:
Load an assembly or application folder and produce an architecture overview.
path, focus?

arguments.name: GUIDE
arguments.description:
The full guidance on one area: dotnet, native, il2cpp, containers, edits, builds, idapython, dump...
topic?

arguments.name: PATCH_NATIVE
arguments.description:
Find the instruction that decides a behaviour, patch it in memory with a preview, and save a patc...
image, goal

arguments.name: EXPLAIN_TYPE
arguments.description:
Explain what a type does, how it is used, and its important members.
type, assembly?

arguments.name: INVESTIGATE_FEATURE
arguments.description:
From a behaviour the user describes to the code behind it, with the evidence recorded, the unknow...
behaviour, target?, evidencePath?

arguments.name: ANALYZE_NATIVE
arguments.description: Load a native PE file (.exe/.dll/.sys) and produce an overview: what it is, how it is built and h...

arguments.name: GETTING_STARTED
arguments.description: How this server works and a first session on a file of your choice.

arguments.name: FIND_API_USAGE
arguments.description:
Every call site of an imported function and what the callers pass and do with the result.
image, api
check_reimplementation Run a native function believed to compute something on chosen inputs in the emulator and compare...
image, function, computes, cases?

arguments.name: COMPARE_BUILDS
arguments.description:
What changed between two builds of an application (assemblies or native images), and carry existi...
oldPath, newPath, focus?

arguments.name: MAP_NATIVE_ADDRESS
arguments.description:
Identify the managed method behind a native address from IDA/Ghidra or a crash log (IL2CPP builds).
address, dummyDllFolder?

arguments.name: TRACE_NATIVE_FEATURE
arguments.description:
Find the native code behind a behaviour, from strings, APIs and constants to the deciding function.
feature, image
15 prompts. Render one: corvus prompt <name> name=value ...

commands.name: resources
commands.description: List resources and templates; read <uri> prints one.

commands.name: status
commands.description:
Read-only check. Starts each client's registered command with that entry's own args
and env, checks this build's server and tool catalog (digest), the engines, and
installed skills (aligned with this build, or stale).
--client X      only these clients (fails only for them)
--engine E      only ida, python, ghidra or all (--deep also starts IDA's worker)
--target PATH   what the file is and which engines read it
--json          the report as JSON

commands.name: update
commands.description:
Install the latest release (installed copies only) and refresh existing registrations;
it never adds clients.
--version X     install release X instead, also an older one (rollback)
--dry-run       show the release, asset and checksum manifest it would use
